summary: 120-foot Alabama Forestry Commission tower in Baldwin County, built 1942 and removed by early 2018; a 2013 sale to New York is also reported.

facts.design: 120-foot tower; NHLR says International Derrick with 7-by-7-foot cab, Forest Lookouts says Aermotor MC-39
facts.status_note: NHLR says removed by early 2018; Forest Lookouts says sold, dismantled and shipped to New York in 2013

access.note: No standing tower is recorded at the site

events.note: Started by the CCC and completed by the Alabama Forestry Commission
Forest Lookouts: sold, dismantled and shipped to New York for restoration and resale
NHLR: removed by early 2018; former-site photo shows footings from April 2018

evidence.supports: administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission
started by the CCC, completed by the commission in 1942
evidence.quote: started by the CCC and completed by the Alabama Foresry Commission in 1942

evidence.supports: design: 120-foot International Derrick tower with 7-by-7-foot cab
evidence.quote: It was a 120' International Derrick tower with a 7'x7' cab.
The tower was removed by early 2018.

evidence.supports: photo of tower footings dated April 2018
120-foot Aermotor MC-39 sold, dismantled, shipped to New York for restoration and resale
evidence.quote: The 120-foot Aermotor MC-39 tower was sold, dismantled and shipped to New York, where the tower is undergoing restoration and future resale.

corrections.why: NHLR and the former-site listing both say the tower was removed by early 2018; the photo shows footings from April 2018

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR describes a 120-foot International Derrick tower with a 7-by-7-foot cab; Forest Lookouts describes a 120-foot Aermotor MC-39. Both are recorded; neither is chosen.

Forest Lookouts gives a 2013 sale, dismantling and shipment to New York; NHLR and the former-site listing give removal by early 2018, with footings photographed April 2018. Both dates are kept and the story says the accounts differ.

notes_for_editor: No staffing, notable fire or access sources found. The make of the tower and the removal date conflict across sources and the story reports both. The 2013 sale to New York rests on Forest Lookouts alone. Two WebSearch-era leads were checked; none added a source beyond the three above. Brief's status 'standing' is wrong: both NHLR and FFLOS say removed.
